entry.title: Quotes I Like
entry.content:
Over time, I have collected a few quotes that stay with me. They are not conclusions, but small reminders that shift meaning depending on the moment. Some I have traced back through others, while others I do not know where I first heard them. When I know the source, I include the name.

“The tallest tree gets the wind.”

— Zhuo Fan (The Steward Demonic Emperor)
This resonates with my understanding of a broader Chinese mindset that values modesty, balance, and staying low rather than seeking prominence.

“Their memory serves as an example to us all!
The courageous fallen! The anguished fallen!
Their lives have meaning because we, the living, refuse to forget them!
And as we ride to certain death, we trust our successors to do the same for us!”

— Erwin Smith (Attack on Titan (Shingeki no Kyojin))

“A king never wavers, never bends, never relies on others, and never gives up.”

— Qin Shi Huang (Record of Ragnarok)

“Wherever I sit, that place shall become my throne.”

— Qin Shi Huang (Record of Ragnarok)

“80 percent of success is showing up.”

— usually attributed to Woody Allen

“Drinking wine and being joyful is my creed;
Being free from both unbelief and religion is my religion.
I asked the Bride of Time: ‘What is your dowry?’
She answered: ‘Your cheerful heart is my dowry.’”

— Omar Khayyam

“What’s the biggest lie you were ever told?
— It’s not that simple.
No, that’s the biggest lie I was ever told: ‘It’s not that simple.’
And it’s a lie they tell you over and over again.
What’s not simple? Any of it. All of it.
It’s how they get you to give up.”

— Vinny Pazienza (Bleed for This)

“Kids who have never seen peace and kids who have never seen war have different values.”

— Donquixote Doflamingo (One Piece, Marineford Arc)

“Next time you think you are making an independent choice, ask yourself: who benefits from this choice I make?
Did I really choose, or did someone engineer it in my mind and choose it for me?”

“Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake.”

— usually attributed to Napoleon Bonaparte
Often misattributed to Sun Tzu’s The Art of War, where it does not appear.

“Why would I chase a glacier when there’s a perfectly good sunshine right in front of me?”

“Did I owe the entire Milky Way money to end up with this?”

I return to these lines not for answers, but for perspective. Each time I read them, they feel slightly different. Some are attributed to real people, while others come from anime, manga, or manhwa, but I find meaning in all of them in the same way.
entry.summary: A small collection of quotes I return to from time to time.

entry.title: My Connection to Persian and Iranian Languages

link.title: My Connection to Persian and Iranian Languages

entry.content:
Persian and its sister languages hold a very special place in my heart. Growing up in a household adorned with countless old books, especially poetry collections, I was captivated by the literary world from an early age. As a child, I would often find solace in solitude, sitting quietly and immersing myself in the verses of Rumi, Khayyam, Rudaki, and Khaqani. It was an enchanting experience that I still yearn to relive.

To this day, poetry remains an important part of my life, and one of the websites I especially enjoy visiting is Ganjoor, a remarkable archive of Persian poetry. This deep personal connection evolved into a lasting passion for language, culture, and meaning, which eventually led me toward multilingual NLP. I feel especially fortunate to have had the opportunity to work on multilingual NLP during my PhD, including research involving Persian and related languages.

Beyond my professional work, in my free time I also lead an open-source community focused on Iranian languages through SIGIranic, where we work to support resources, tools, and collaboration for these languages.
entry.summary: A personal reflection on my connection to Persian poetry, multilingual NLP, and open-source work on Iranian languages.
